titleEn: A Bite of Green, a Bite of White!

pages.text: "Green goes over there." Riri, in her yellow hat, picked the green pieces out of her soup. They lined up around her plate. Beside her, Lolo in yellow boots slurped—the bowl was already half empty.

"Tomorrow morning, I want to pull Dad's rope by myself!" Riri waved her spoon. Mom, who ran the fish stall, set down the pot and looked at her bowl. The green row grew longer, and only half the soup remained.
The next morning, Dad's boat was about to leave. Riri gripped the rope mooring it and strained. It would not budge. "Strange. Where did my strength go?"
That evening, Mom made fish soup again. "Riri, where do you think this green came from?" Riri tilted her head. "...I do not know."
"Seaweed Dad gathered from the shore rocks." Mom held up a strand. "The waves rocked it as it grew, so it is strong." Riri sniffed the salty scent of the sea.
Mom placed one white piece of fish and one green piece side by side on a spoon. "They are a pair. A bite of green, a bite of white!" Matching pairs was Riri's favorite thing.
Riri counted on her fingers. "One white, one green. Two!" She put the spoonful in her mouth. Salty and tasty. "...Oh? It is delicious!"
Morning came again. Riri held the rope with both hands. Strain—slide! The rope slipped toward her. "See? I did it myself!" Riri called, and Lolo clapped.
That evening, Riri picked up her spoon first. "One, do not pick out the green! Two, pair green with white and take a bite! Three, finish to the bottom!" Today, the plate's rim was empty.
Mom wiped Riri's mouth with her blue apron and touched foreheads with her. Eating different foods gave Riri strength to pull the rope alone. "A bite of green, a bite of white!" Riri raised her spoon.
